name: Core AI vocabulary, Polish
summary: 349 Polish terms (162 of tier `ai`, 187 of tier `context`) in the 13 groups of the English core glossary (core.json), for wordings that core.json does not match: Polish terms, Polish case forms of English loanwords (chatbota, promptów, deepfake'ów), wording of Polish and EU law in its Polish text, and stand-ins for AI in Polish corporate reports. It applies only to filings whose language is pl, together with core.json, which matches the English terms these filings use unchanged (AI, machine learning, ChatGPT); English entries that Polish reports use unchanged are therefore not repeated here. Case forms (singular and plural) are listed as variants, because the plural suffix that glossary.py adds is the English one, and each form is also listed without Polish diacritics for text extracted from PDF. Built by going through all 502 entries of core.json and keeping a Polish wording only if it, or another case form of it, occurs in a source that was read: the Polish text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, of the GDPR, the Digital Services Act and the DSM copyright directive, the EU terminology database IATE, publications of UKNF, UOKiK, NASK, the Financial Ombudsman and the Ministry of Digital Affairs, the bill on AI systems (Sejm print 2443), Polish business press, 33 management and annual reports of Warsaw-listed companies for 2024 and 2025 and the six Polish reports in gs://airo-eu-sample-reports. Tier `ai` terms whose hits in these reports were mostly not about AI were moved to `context` or removed. Checked on 37 Polish annual reports of 2025 from 19 ISIC sections (gs://airo-eu-sample-reports/sector-sample): the bare noun przekwalifikowanie was removed and a term for service robots was added. Status: draft; to be checked by a native speaker.
